        CONCAT '-' CONCAT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM valid_from)
    ) AS valid_from
    FROM some_table NOLOCK

Q: If product code does not exist in first part of query pull a declared value from another table for that product code A: 
SELECT 
    COALESCE(spr.Price, psb.SellPrice) AS Price, 
    Per.PerCode, 
    p.ProductCode, 
    p.Description
FROM Product p

-- get the specific customer to use in our exact pricing join
LEFT JOIN customer c 
    ON c.CustomerCode = '7000192'

-- get the specific price rule for this exact customer
LEFT JOIN SellPriceRule spr 
    ON p.ProductID = spr.ProductID 
    AND spr.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

-- get the fallback price band (Band 8 for AB region)
LEFT JOIN ProductSellPriceBand psb 
    ON p.ProductID = psb.ProductID 
    AND psb.BandNumber = 8 
    AND psb.Description LIKE 'AB%'

-- get the PerCode based on whichever table provided the price
LEFT JOIN Per 
    ON Per.PerID = COALESCE(spr.PricePerID, psb.PerID)

-- filter for the specific products you are looking for
WHERE p.ProductCode IN (
    '27MIETE10B',
    '22RGR45DHS',
    '23RGWBBCA',
    '22RGED4WA',
    '22RGED45WA'
)

It's difficult to do what you're asking for due to the lack of the original data tables.

I did it as it should be in theory. If anything's wrong, please leave a comment and I'll edit it.

Adding an aggregate function like MIN() absolutely requires grouping the rest of selected columns using a GROUP BY clause. However, there is a common trap to watch out for here: if a product happens to have two rules for the same customer with different prices, a standard GROUP BY will output a duplicate row for that product (one for each price) instead of picking the single "winning" rule.

As I see you have used [dbo] you must be using SQL Server, so there is better solution - to swap the LEFT JOIN for an OUTER APPLY:

SELECT 
    COALESCE(spr.Price, psb.SellPrice) AS Price, 
    Per.PerCode, 
    p.ProductCode, 
    p.Description,
    spr.RulePriority AS RulePrio
FROM Product p

LEFT JOIN customer c 
    ON c.CustomerCode = '7000192'

-- takes ONLY the single highest-priority rule for this product & customer
OUTER APPLY (
    SELECT TOP 1 Price, PricePerID, RulePriority
    FROM SellPriceRule
    WHERE ProductID = p.ProductID 
      AND CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    ORDER BY RulePriority ASC -- assuming lower number = higher priority
) spr

LEFT JOIN ProductSellPriceBand psb 
    ON p.ProductID = psb.ProductID 
    AND psb.BandNumber = 8 
    AND psb.Description LIKE 'AB%'

LEFT JOIN Per 
    ON Per.PerID = COALESCE(spr.PricePerID, psb.PerID)

WHERE p.ProductCode IN (
    '27MIETE10B',
    '22RGR45DHS',
    '23RGWBBCA',
    '22RGED4WA',
    '22RGED45WA'
);

Q: Regex pattern produces unexpected result A:

Explanation

Replace all works by repeatedly applying the pattern against the text. Easy to verify with this content

aaa

Then doing a replace all of ^a with nothing. That would normally only match one. But if you repeatedly apply the replacement, then after the first one the content is

aa

Which matches ^a again, replacing leaves

a

Which matches ^a again, replacing leaves nothing.

In the same way replacing ^(\s+\S+) with empty leaves an empty line. For input like:

    -Foo
-Bar

The result is a blank line followed by another line of text:


-Bar

And that is then matched again by ^(\s+\S+) as it is \n-Bar - any amount of whitespace at the start of the line (single newline on line 1) followed by any amount of non-whitespace ("-Bar" on line 2). This is because \s consumes newlines, so it will do a multiline match.

Alternatives

Change the regex

Remove lines content, leaves empty lines

To avoid matching empty lines use ^(?!\r?\n)(\s+\S+)

Putting (?!\r?\n) at the start will skip lines that start with a newline character. However, the replace all will still leave a blank line resulting in


-ExcludeProperty
-ExpandProperty


-InputObject

-Property



-Unique
-Wait

Those can be removed by going to Edit -> Line Operations -> Remove Empty Lines.

Remove whole lines

Use ^(?:\r?\n|(\s+\S+)).

This matches any empty line or line that starts with whitespace. Thus, if it gets repeatedly applied, it will remove blank lines but not match content on the following line.

Mark and remove

You can keep the same regex but instead

  1. Go to the "Mark" tab in the search tool (Ctrl+M or switch from the "Find" or the "Replace" tabs in the search tool).
  2. Check "Bookmark line".
  3. Enter the regex you want.
  4. Click "Mark All".

This marks the lines which match, they can then be deleted by going to: Search (from the top menu) -> Bookmark -> Remove bookmarked lines. There is also "Remove non-bookmarked lines" if you want to leave any lines that match a regex.

Q: Reverse engineer of APC UPS serial protocol A:

There's currently experimental Microlink support in NUT. NUT is the Network UPS Tools open source project. From the NUT manual:

CONFIGURATION

The driver is configured via ups.conf(5).

A minimal configuration:

[apc-microlink]
    driver = apcmicrolink
    port = /dev/ttyUSB0

Q: Trying to control step motor with LCD and Raspberry Pi Pico 2 A:

The GPIO pin may not be able to source enough current to drive the motor. You should use a logic level MOSFET/BJT to switch it instead, then connect the GPIO pin to the gate/base through an appropriate resistor. Also, the motor is an inductive load, the voltage spikes when it is switched off could damage your Pico. You should add a reverse biased (connected "backwards", cathode to +, anode to -) diode such as 1N4007 across your motor.
